options.name: Dauphin Island Campground
options.priceNote: $22/night tent (year-round) + 5% maintenance fee + 11% lodging tax = ~$25.60 total; reservations require a 2-night non-refundable deposit, so walk-up as-available is simpler for one night
options.locationNote: On Dauphin Island, ~0.5 mi from the Mobile Bay Ferry landing and Fort Gaines; requires crossing the bay (last ferry from Fort Morgan 3:30 PM)
options.legalityNote: Town-run 151-site public campground; fully legal, tent sites back onto the Audubon Bird Sanctuary
options.cyclistIntel: Classic Southern Tier stop — riders roll off the ferry straight into the campground; island is very bike-friendly. Tent sites have water/electric. Gate house open 7 AM-6:30 PM (7 PM Fri/Sat)
options.seasonalNote: Sept is 'winter season' rate period; late Sept is peak hurricane season — ferry suspends in winds >35 mph, have a bail-out plan

options.name: Gulf State Park Campground (primitive tent loop)
options.priceNote: $25/night primitive tent-only sites 501-508 (tent pad, fire pit, table; no hookups) + reservation fee/taxes; full-hookup sites run $50-90+
options.locationNote: In Gulf Shores, ~2 mi north of the beach road; ~17-18 route miles BEFORE the Day 1 endpoint (shorten the day)
options.legalityNote: Alabama state park; tents welcome on all 496 sites plus the 8 primitive tent-only sites
options.cyclistIntel: The route threads Gulf State Park's paved Backcountry Trail system, so the campground is essentially on-route; common first/last Alabama night for Southern Tier riders
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; post-Labor Day availability is good

options.name: Southport Campground
options.priceNote: Tent/primitive sites offered per Gulf Shores tourism listing; current tent rate unpublished (est. $25-35, RV sites ~$40s) — call to confirm; website was unreachable Aug 2026
options.locationNote: Under the Intracoastal Waterway bridge on the north edge of Gulf Shores, ~12 mi before endpoint
options.legalityNote: Established private campground advertising RV and tent camping with hot showers and clean restrooms
options.cyclistIntel: No specific touring-cyclist reports found; nearby Doc's RV (mi 68.6) is explicitly NO tents and Island Retreat is $64+/RV-focused, so this is the tent-friendly pick of the mile-66-69 cluster

options.name: Fort Morgan RV Park
options.priceNote: Tents allowed per Good Sam/Hipcamp listings but rates not published (RV full-hookup sites listed 'from $93' on Hipcamp; likely $50+ for any site) — call and ask for a one-night tent-camper rate
options.locationNote: 10397 2nd St on Bon Secour Bay, ~1 mi from the Fort Morgan ferry landing — only camping within striking distance of the 8:00 AM boat
options.legalityNote: Established 34-site private park; listings say 'tent campers, car campers, pop-ups welcome'
options.cyclistIntel: Strategic rather than cheap: camping here guarantees the 8:00 AM ferry. Fort Morgan historic site itself has no camping

gapAdvice: The planned endpoint (mi 78.1) sits in a camping dead zone between the Gulf Shores cluster (mi 60-69) and the ferry (mi ~86). Best play: lengthen ~9 mi, catch the LAST 3:30 PM ferry from Fort Morgan (departures 8:00/10:30/1:00/3:30; bikes free, pedestrian fare ~$5-10; verify at mobilebayferry.com, (251) 540-7787) and camp at Dauphin Island Campground for $22 — you also bank the crossing against morning weather cancellation. If you can't make 3:30, call Fort Morgan RV Park (pricey) for the 8:00 AM boat, or shorten to Gulf State Park's $25 primitive loop and ride 25 mi to the 10:30 AM ferry.

options.name: Shepard State Park (primitive tent areas)
options.priceNote: Primitive tent camping $13/night (3 first-come areas, 3-day max); developed W/E sites historically $18 but a Feb 2025 camper reported $38 ($33 senior/military) — confirm primitive rate by phone
options.locationNote: 1034 Graveline Rd, Gautier — ~5 route miles past Pascagoula, ~1 mi off US 90
options.legalityNote: State park (city-operated); primitive tent camping explicitly 'allowed and encouraged'
options.cyclistIntel: Long-running budget stop for Southern Tier riders along the MS coast; restrooms/bathhouses on site, quiet pine woods
options.seasonalNote: Open; park website advises checking operating status before arrival (phone lines were down mid-2026)

options.name: Davis Bayou Campground (Gulf Islands National Seashore)
options.priceNote: NPS campground (type approximated): $20 standard non-electric / $22 electric per night via recreation.gov; 50% off with federal Senior/Access pass
options.locationNote: 3500 Park Rd, Ocean Springs — ~17 route miles past Pascagoula (use the +flex to set up a shorter Day 3)
options.legalityNote: National Park Service campground, 52 sites, open year-round
options.cyclistIntel: Reliable federal campground with hot showers; popular with coast-riding tourers as the Ocean Springs overnight
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; late-Sept mosquitoes on the bayou can be fierce — bring repellent

gapAdvice: Pascagoula itself has no legal campground — plan on Shepard SP 5 mi ahead in Gautier ($13 primitive) or push 17 mi to Davis Bayou. The OSM 'RV Campground' at mi 153.8 is Indian Point RV Resort (Gautier, $40/night) which is RVs-ONLY, no tents — skip it.

options.name: Buccaneer State Park (Royal Cay primitive area)
options.priceNote: ~$20/night primitive tent (25 sites, restrooms within 100 yds); reservable developed tent sites $28; RV sites $28-40
options.locationNote: 1150 S Beach Blvd, Waveland, on the beachfront — ~10-12 mi south of the Diamondhead endpoint; the route detours INLAND at Pass Christian toward Picayune, so this is an off-route coastal detour you'd have to un-ride next morning
options.legalityNote: Mississippi state park; primitive tent area is first-come, developed sites via ReserveAmerica
options.cyclistIntel: Was the standard MS-coast overnight on the old US-90 Southern Tier alignment; multiple bathhouses. Cheapest verified-legal bed of the day
options.seasonalNote: Late Sept is shoulder season (Cruisin' the Coast crowds arrive early Oct); hurricane-watch closures possible

options.name: McLeod Park Campground (Hancock County)
options.priceNote: $35/night non-waterfront, $45 waterfront — all 120 sites are full-hookup county-park sites; tents accepted per camper listings (confirm when booking)
options.locationNote: 8100 Texas Flat Rd on the Jourdan River near Kiln — ~4-5 mi from Diamondhead and near the inland detour toward Picayune
options.legalityNote: Hancock County public park campground; camper-only bathhouse with hot showers, ADA-accessible
options.cyclistIntel: The practical on-route choice for the Diamondhead/Kiln overnight — no backtrack, right at the top of your $35 ceiling. Older $23-26 riverside rates are gone since the 2020s rebuild

options.name: Bay Hide Away RV Park & Campground
options.priceNote: RV standard from $49; has only 5 tent sites 'available upon request' — tent rate unpublished, may be lower; call
options.locationNote: 8360 Lakeshore Rd, Bay St. Louis/Lakeshore — well south of the inland detour (~14 mi off endpoint)
options.legalityNote: Family-owned private campground; tents allowed on request
options.cyclistIntel: Immaculate bathhouses per reviews; realistically a backup only given price and location

gapAdvice: Diamondhead proper has no campground, and Hollywood Casino RV Park (Bay St. Louis) is RVs-only. McLeod ($35, 4-5 mi away, no backtrack) is the practical pick; Buccaneer's $20 primitive area saves $15 but costs a ~20-mi round-trip detour off the inland reroute. Decide by legs, not wallet.

options.name: Berry Creek Cabins (tent/RV area)
options.priceNote: Advertises tent camping + full-hookup RV sites with two bathhouses; nightly tent rate unpublished (est. $20-30) — call (985) 730-4395 before committing
options.locationNote: 12101 George Jenkins Rd E (Bogalusa address), off the LA-21 corridor ~2-4 mi before Sun; near Bogue Chitto River tubing outfits
options.legalityNote: Established private cabin/RV/tent operation on 7 acres in Washington Parish
options.cyclistIntel: Only sleep-spot essentially ON route at the Sun endpoint (OSM tags it at mi 261); cabins from ~$100+ if storms roll in
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; office hours 9 AM-9 PM daily

options.name: Fontainebleau State Park
options.priceNote: Unimproved tent sites in the LA $18-27+tax band (250+ unimproved sites, 33 designated tent sites, mostly first-come); improved W/E sites $28-42+tax + $4.50 reservation fee
options.locationNote: Mandeville, on Lake Pontchartrain — ~20 route miles past Sun (lengthen the day, shorten tomorrow's run into NOLA)
options.legalityNote: Louisiana state park, open year-round; tent camping is a core offering
options.cyclistIntel: Sits directly on the Tammany Trace rail-trail — the North Shore cycling corridor — and is a frequent tourer camp; flush restrooms and showers at the tent areas
options.seasonalNote: Fully reopened post-Ida; recent 2026 reviews confirm operational. Hurricane-season closures possible on tropical warnings

options.name: Bogue Chitto State Park
options.priceNote: Improved W/E campsites $25-33+tax + $4.50 reservation fee; tent camping welcome on sites
options.locationNote: 17049 State Park Blvd near Franklinton — ~13 hilly road miles NW of Sun via LA-10/LA-25; off-route detour both ways
options.legalityNote: Louisiana state park; reservations via gooutdoorslouisiana.com or 877-226-7652
options.cyclistIntel: Beautiful river-bluff park with 25 mi of trails, but the 26-mi round-trip detour makes it a fallback rather than a plan

gapAdvice: Thin day. Bogalusa has NO legal camping (Cassidy Park is day-use only). Call Berry Creek from Bogalusa; if no answer or no tents, the honest choices are the 13-mi detour to Bogue Chitto SP or riding +20 to Fontainebleau's first-come tent sites ($18-27) — the latter also turns Day 5 into an easy ~52-mi cruise into New Orleans.

options.name: St. Bernard State Park
options.priceNote: Improved W/E sites $20-28+tax (Fri 9/25 = $28) + $4.50 reservation fee; 50% off with America the Beautiful pass (out-of-state honored per LA reciprocity rules)
options.locationNote: Braithwaite, ~18 mi SE of downtown along the Mississippi — overshoots the city on the East Bank/Chalmette side (Chalmette ferry option)
options.legalityNote: Louisiana state park with partial-hookup RV and tent camping
options.cyclistIntel: Quieter than Bayou Segnette but the approach roads (LA-39/LA-46) carry fast traffic; only worth it if continuing downriver next day
options.seasonalNote: Year-round; low-lying — closes on flood/tropical warnings

options.name: India House Hostel
options.priceNote: Dorm beds from ~$29-40 depending on night (Fri 9/25 will be the higher end); shared kitchen, courtyard; not camping but the cheapest legal in-city bed
options.locationNote: 124 S Lopez St, Mid-City — ~2 mi from the downtown endpoint, right off Canal St streetcar
options.legalityNote: Licensed backpacker hostel; bike storage usually available in the courtyard (confirm)
options.cyclistIntel: Longtime budget standby for touring cyclists finishing/starting Gulf legs in NOLA; sociable, secure enough for a loaded bike

options.name: Bayou Segnette State Park
options.priceNote: $33+tax Fri-Sat ($30 Sun-Thu Apr-Sep) + $4.50 reservation fee; 98 improved W/E sites, tents welcome
options.locationNote: Westwego on the West Bank — ~mi 344, 3.5 mi off route; from downtown take the Canal St-Algiers Point ferry (bikes OK, ~$2-3) then ~10 mi west
options.legalityNote: Louisiana state park; standard legal camping closest to New Orleans
options.cyclistIntel: THE stock answer to 'camping near NOLA' among tourers — ferry + West Bank ride is the accepted bike approach; wave pool and clean comfort stations

options.name: New Orleans KOA Holiday (River Ridge)
options.priceNote: Tent sites $60-98/night — far over budget; listed only because it's the one campground on the route's River Rd approach (mi 348)
options.locationNote: 11129 Jefferson Hwy, River Ridge, near the Mississippi levee path ~13 mi upriver of downtown
options.cyclistIntel: Levee bike path runs nearby into the city; convenient but the price makes it a last resort

gapAdvice: There is no camping in New Orleans proper — every tent option overshoots or detours: Bayou Segnette ($33+tax, cross via Algiers Point ferry then ~10 mi), St. Bernard SP ($28, 18 mi SE), KOA ($60+). For a rest day IN the city, India House Hostel (~$29-40 dorm, Mid-City, (504) 821-1904) beats the ferry-and-ride logistics and costs about the same as a Friday-night state-park site; HI New Orleans and The Quisby run ~$40+. If camping matters more than the city, book Bayou Segnette online before arrival — Friday nights fill.
